A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CI/CSM research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, appendices A–E and checklist support reliable comparison despite reordering.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation experiments across eight datasets and two LLM backbones, training ablations, CI analyses and appendix case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds agentic baseline results and inference-latency measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix B retain the same CI selection rule, hierarchical CSM, data interventions, supervised losses and differentiable end-to-end training. Figure 2's revised labels and arrangement do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: The same eight datasets, task families and Wikipedia retrieval corpus are used. The added latency experiment uses existing NQ, TriviaQA and HotpotQA coverage; the TruthfulQA split revision and retrieval budgets concern experimental settings.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated Self-RAG and RQ-RAG baselines across all eight datasets and both backbones while retaining existing comparators. This substantially broadens the main comparison to agentic retrieval and generation approaches; Self-RAG was previously cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: The dataset-statistics table changes TruthfulQA train/dev/test counts from 653/82/82 to 327/82/408, without establishing whether experiments were rerun. New Table 3 measures selection-to-generation CUDA latency at 10 and 50 retrieved contexts, matching baseline retained-context counts to 5 and 23 respectively. Existing generation metrics and the main top-k=5 comparison remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.2 adds a scalability analysis testing latency as retrieved-context count increases from 10 to 50. The training ablations, CI distributions, context-addition curves and three appendix case studies are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify the fixed random seed 2024 in Appendix C.3. V2 introduces no additional repeated-run information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial comparative and efficiency evidence. In Table 1, RQ-RAG becomes the highest non-oracle Llama3-8B WebQA entry at 26.12, versus CSM-e2e's retained 26.05. New Table 3 reports NQ latency at 50 contexts of 481 ms for CSM, 1437 ms for RankGPT and 662 ms for RECOMP-abs. All shared Table 1 scores remain numerically unchanged, while both average-improvement rows are removed.

T1.justification: Definition 1, the utility and subset-selection formulations, training objectives and Appendix B intervention equation are unchanged. No new assumptions, theoretical results or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same CI contribution, four desired properties, hierarchical surrogate and two training approaches. The headline 15.03% average improvement claim also remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 newly interprets the agentic comparisons as showing greater benefits from filtering poor contexts than from complex reflection and planning. It also attributes the latency advantage to CSM's lightweight architecture and better scaling with context count. The task-specific training and generalization limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds timing-specific reproducibility information: CUDA measurement spans context selection through generation, with retained-context counts matched to CSM's average positive-context count. Existing architecture details, training hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds the RQ-RAG reference and positions CSM empirically against RQ-RAG and the already-cited Self-RAG. The dedicated related-work discussion otherwise retains its original scope and arguments.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized baseline-description edits, replaces generic supplementary-material pointers with specific appendix references, corrects the duplicated university name and adds acknowledgements. The checklist moves before the appendices, while the main scientific narrative remains largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains agentic-baseline rows and loses average-improvement rows, and a new latency table is added. Figures 1–2 receive localized visual revisions, particularly Figure 2's training labels and arrangement. Appendix tables are renumbered and Figure 11 is repositioned; existing analytical plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The agentic comparisons and previously absent latency/scaling measurements strengthen assessment of CSM's competitiveness and practical cost. The gains are limited by reporting ambiguities: TruthfulQA's split changes without explanation or changed shared scores, and the 15.03% headline remains after its supporting average-improvement rows are removed. Overall, v2 provides useful additional evidence without resolving these consistency issues.
